detail.abstract: On 11 June 2026, Kazakhstan enacted Law No. 306-VIII, removing-with effect from 1 January 2027-the state's inflation-indexation guarantee on mandatory pension contributions in the Unified Accumulative Pension Fund (ENPF), so that only nominal contribution values remain protected. The legislative record examined here shows the change was never introduced as pension policy: the provisions entered through in-passage amendment of a bill originally confined to electoral law, with no published explanatory note, and were enacted inside an omnibus constitutional-alignment statute. This paper situates the reform within the comparative literature on funded-pension privatization reversals and argues that deindexation constitutes a second-order retrenchment: an incremental erosion of state obligations occurring inside an already re-nationalized system, a stage the canonical Hungarian, Polish, and Argentine cases did not reach because their reversals terminated the private pillar outright. Using a theory-testing process-tracing design in which the sovereigndebt-exposure account of reversal supplies the mechanism and Russia's post-2014 contribution moratorium serves as a quantified calibration case, the paper develops and defends a fiscal-substitution interpretation: persistent negative real returns on ENPF assets in 2025-2026 made the inflation guarantee an open-ended contingent liability precisely as National Fund transfers were being compressed, and de-indexation extinguishes that liability while preserving the contribution inflow. An event-window analysis of KASE governmentbond yield indices around the 11 June 2026 announcement finds no economically significant sovereign repricing-a null consistent with the captive-demand structure of the ENPF portfolio and locating the reform's fiscal benefit in liability extinction rather than bond-market pricing. Three falsifiable predictions are derived for post-2027 observation: increased allocation of ENPF assets to sovereign and quasi-sovereign instruments, tightened earlywithdrawal rules, and further incremental guarantee erosion within two to four electoralfiscal cycles. Because the reform takes effect in 2027, the paper is explicitly predictive rather than retrospective; its claims are structured to be testable against outcome data as it emerges.

title: Self-Fulfilling Prediction Markets: A Theory of Reflexive Prices

detail.title: Self-Fulfilling Prediction Markets: A Theory of Reflexive Prices
detail.abstract: Prediction-market prices are increasingly consulted by institutions whose actions move the outcomes on which the contracts settle, making the equilibrium price a fixed point of the response it triggers. We characterize the resulting equilibrium. Transparent responses leave price informativeness unchanged; erosion requires response risk, which we derive from the decision maker's own information, and influence times precision then obeys an exact bound. Discrete responses generate self-fulfilling multiplicity whose signature, an empty band in the price distribution, is estimable from a single contract's price history, validated on placebo and adversarial data. Optimal institutions choose interior opacity; the welfare instrument taxes reliance in calm regimes and can become a subsidy when crisis-state determinacy benefits dominate.

title: Tax Competition After the Floor: Cantonal Responses to the Global Minimum Tax in Switzerland

detail.title: Tax Competition After the Floor: Cantonal Responses to the Global Minimum Tax in Switzerland

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human subjects, personal data, or primary data collection requiring informed consent. The empirical strategy relies exclusively on: (i) publicly available and commercially licensed administrative and firm-level financial data (Swiss Federal Tax Administration statistics, OECD Country-by-Country Reporting aggregates, and Orbis/Bureau van Dijk firm-level records), all of which are anonymized, aggregated, or governed by existing commercial data-use licenses; and (ii) computationally simulated data generated for the purpose of validating the estimation pipeline, as described in Section 6. No individual-level personal, medical, or identifying information is collected, processed, or disclosed. Accordingly, this research does not require institutional ethics board (IRB) review under standard economics research protocols. Should the study be extended to include primary data collection (e.g., surveys of cantonal officials or firm representatives), appropriate ethics approval will be sought prior to that data collection commencing.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted independently as part of the author's academic research programme at Lagos State University, Nigeria.

detail.abstract: The OECD/G20 Pillar Two agreement introduces a 15 percent global minimum effective tax rate (ETR) for large multinational enterprises (MNEs), removing the statutory tax rate as the primary instrument of sub-national tax competition in federal states. Switzerland, whose 26 cantons have historically competed on headline corporate tax rates, offers a uniquely clean setting to study how sub-national governments substitute across policy instruments once a supranational floor constrains their principal lever. This paper develops an empirical strategy to identify the causal effect of Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax (QDMTT) adoption on cantonal fiscal policyspecifically, substitution toward non-rate instruments such as R&D superdeductions, patent boxes, and location subsidies-using a staggered difference-indifferences design applied to canton-level administrative tax data and firm-level data on multinational subsidiaries operating in Switzerland. We outline the institutional background, situate the question within the tax competition and fiscal federalism literatures, specify a identification strategy robust to heterogeneous treatment timing, and derive testable hypotheses regarding the magnitude and distribution of instrument substitution across cantons of differing size and pre-reform tax rates. We close with a discussion of data feasibility, expected contributions, and policy relevance for Swiss fiscal authorities and the broader Pillar Two "stocktake" process that the OECD Inclusive Framework has built into the agreement itself. To confirm the identification strategy is computationally tractable ahead of real-data collection, the full estimation pipeline fixed-effects triple-differences, event study, and bunching estimator-is implemented in Python from first principles and executed on a calibrated simulated panel; the pipeline runs without error and recovers the calibrated parameters, and the code is available for direct application to the real Orbis/ESTV panel once assembled.

title: Sui Generis Licensing and The Green Retrofit: A Case Study of Ccus Integration at the Dangote Refinery
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Sui Generis Licensing and The Green Retrofit: A Case Study of Ccus Integration at the Dangote Refinery
detail.abstract: The commissioning of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery in Lagos, the largest single-train crude oil refinery in the world exposes a structural gap in international intellectual property law that has received little scholarly attention, the absence of a licensing framework adequate to the demands of carbon capture, utilisation, and storage (CCUS) retrofits in complex industrial settings. Conventional patent licensing regimes were built around discrete, stable inventions, not the layered, interdependent architecture of a green retrofit, where patented equipment, proprietary process adaptations, and embedded trade secrets must function together across an operating facility. This mismatch leaves technology owners overexposed , host states underprotected, and deployment slower than the climate imperative allows. This article develops the concept of sui generis licensing as the appropriate legal category for the green retrofit context: a bespoke, composite instrument combining elements of patent licensing, trade secret protection, know-how transfer, and public-law concession arrangements into a single coherent framework. Using the Dangote Refinery as a case study, the article examines the technical, regulatory, and geopolitical conditions shaping CCUS integration in Nigeria, and proposes a model licensing architecture designed to reconcile two goals typically treated as being in tension: commercially viable technology deployment and climate-driven technology diffusion to the Global South. The analysis is grounded in Nigerian domestic law, the TRIPS Agreement, the Paris Agreement Technology Mechanism, and the still-emerging international law of climate technology transfer and argues that sui generis licensing offers a replicable template for large-emitter retrofits across other resource-rich developing economies.

title: Predictable but Not Profitable: An Anatomy of the Implementation Gap in LBO Target Prediction

detail.title: Predictable but Not Profitable: An Anatomy of the Implementation Gap in LBO Target Prediction

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests. The author holds no positions in any securities discussed and received no compensation from any entity related to this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: We ask whether the well-documented predictability of leveraged-buyout (LBO) targets translates into investable alpha, using only free public data (SEC EDGAR filings and XBRL financial statements). From 27,072 going-private filings we construct 7,914 deals and 925 high-confidence private-equity takeprivates, and a point-in-time panel of 286,982 firm-quarters. A calibrated gradient-boosted model reproduces the literature: test-set top-decile lift is 4.16x, SHAP directions match prior work, and a missingnessaudit model confirms the signal is feature-driven rather than a coverage artifact. Economically, however, the picture inverts. Announcement premiums parsed from filings (median 33.9%) are real, but highscored firms that are not acquired underperform the market by a median 22%, and all 24 backtest configurations trail the S&P 500 by 6-15 percentage points. An overlay tilt appeared to add value (+2.1 pp), but a pre-registered regime check dismantled it: under a validation-clean model the improvement reverses to -1.9 pp, and the validation-period gain vanishes once the 2020 crash is excluded. Our contributions are (i) a quantitative anatomy of the prediction-profit gap, (ii) documentation of free-data structural limits (delisting-driven survivorship, ticker reuse), and (iii) a validation protocol that catches an artifact others would have banked.

title: The Shift to Trade Secrets in Green Technology: Reconsidering Intellectual Property Strategy in the Climate Transition
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Shift to Trade Secrets in Green Technology: Reconsidering Intellectual Property Strategy in the Climate Transition
detail.abstract: The global push to decarbonise economic activity has driven unprecedented investment in green technology, yet a quiet shift is underway in how that innovation is protected. Patents once served as the default mechanism for safeguarding clean energy and environmental inventions; increasingly, trade secrecy is emerging as the strategic instrument of choice. This article examines that shift through the lens of English and Welsh intellectual property law, situating the analysis within the wider architecture of international technology transfer obligations and climate policy commitments. The article argues that trade secret protection offers real commercial advantages, particularly where patent disclosure requirements sit uneasily alongside competitive positioning in fast-moving green technology markets. But it contends that the growing reliance on secrecy in this sector carries systemic costs that existing scholarship has under-theorised: it slows technology diffusion to the Global South, undermines the disclosure function that patent law was designed to serve, and sits in tension with the collaborative logic of climate governance. Drawing on law-and-economics frameworks, the article develops a reform agenda that preserves legitimate secrecy interests while building structured incentive pathways toward disclosure, particularly in transactions involving public climate finance or technology transfer commitments. The analysis engages with recent case law, the academic literature on innovation incentives, and the evolving legislative landscape under the Trade Secrets (Enforcement, etc) Regulations 2018 and the TRIPS Agreement, offering a framework relevant to both developed-economy legislators and negotiators of climate technology transfer instruments.

title: The Political Ramifications of AI-augmented Work
affiliations: and

detail.title: The Political Ramifications of AI-augmented Work
detail.abstract: Recent advances in AI have fueled concerns about future job displacement and its political consequences for workers at risk. Yet AI is already embedded in the workplace, shaping the daily experiences of millions who use AI tools on the job. We examine how access to AI assistance and direct experience with its capabilities affect workers' behavior and preferences over policy responses to technological change. Using a preregistered field experiment in an online labor market, complemented by evidence from a nationally representative sample of U.S. adults, we find that AI changes how workers perform their jobs and value their labor, but rarely changes what they demand from government. Workers take advantage of AI's immediate benefits but do not connect AI augmentation to the risk of future displacement. Making that connection explicit increases support for adjustment policies such as retraining, but not for restrictions on AI development or use. We discuss what these findings imply about the conditions under which AI generates political backlash.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Skill Demand, and Employment Transformation: Evidence from Pakistan's Labor Market

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence, Skill Demand, and Employment Transformation: Evidence from Pakistan's Labor Market
detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between artificial intelligence adoption, skill demand, and employment transformation in Pakistan's labor market. The primary data was collected from 350 respondents from various sectors across information technology, banking and finance, education, telecommunications, manufacturing, retail and services, healthcare and other sectors using a quantitative research design. The research was conducted using a structured questionnaire, which had four dimensions: AI adoption, AI skills demand, employment transformation, digital literacy, and reskilling readiness. The descriptive results indicated that the respondents perceived there was a high level of skill demand (M=4.12), followed by reskilling readiness (M=4.21), digital literacy (M=4.08), artificial intelligence adoption (M=3.98) and employment transformation (M=3.87). The reliability analysis revealed adequate internal consistency with Cronbach's Alpha scores of 0.70 or higher for all constructs. Correlation analysis found that the adoption of AI had a high positive correlation with Skill Demand (r = 0.712) and Skill Demand with the transformation of employment (r = 0.736). The regression results showed that the adoption of artificial intelligence significantly affected the level of skills demand (β = 0.752, p < 0.001) and employment transformation (β = 0.693, p < 0.001). The results indicate that AI is transforming the workforce: changing skill demands and adopting digital readiness.

title: In-kind Transfer as Self-Selection Mechanism: An Empirical Study
affiliations: University of Essex

detail.title: In-kind Transfer as Self-Selection Mechanism: An Empirical Study
detail.abstract: This paper provides empirical evidence for the theoretical prediction that in-kind transfer programs can improve efficiency through self-targeting. We examine a universal fertility voucher program whose benefits are primarily restricted to housing purchases. The program increases both fertility and housing consumption, with take-up concentrated among households and regions facing the most severe housing constraints. This self-selection substantially improves targeting efficiency, generating significant savings relative to an equivalent unrestricted cash transfer.

title: Price Accuracy and Resolution Capture in Prediction Markets

detail.title: Price Accuracy and Resolution Capture in Prediction Markets
detail.abstract: Prediction markets are praised as accurate and criticized as easy to manipulate. I argue these claims are not in conflict, because a prediction market has two separate parts. A trading layer sets the price, and a resolution layer decides the outcome after the event. The price corrects itself, because a wrong price is a chance to profit and other traders trade against it, but the resolution layer does not, because on platforms like Polymarket it is settled by a token-weighted vote, and a voter can vote for the outcome that pays their own position. Using 2,100 of the highest-volume resolved Polymarket markets, I find that the trading layer is well calibrated, with a regression of outcomes on prices that cannot be distinguished from perfect calibration. The documented capture cases instead cluster in markets with vague resolution rules, with one clear-rule case that points to a second channel through voting power. Because these prices are now used by news outlets and automated systems, a captured resolution is not just money moving between traders but a cost imposed on everyone who relies on the price.

title: Commonality in Sustainability
affiliations: Athens University of Economics and Business - Department of Accounting and Finance, Athens University of Economics and Business - Department of Accounting and Finance and University of Peloponnese

detail.title: Commonality in Sustainability
detail.abstract: We examine sustainability commonality, the alignment of firm-level ESG practices with country, industry, regional, and global sustainability factors, using data from 3,010 firms across 36 markets. ESG alignment is strongest within countries, particularly in the environmental and social pillars. The 2015 Paris Agreement served as a global shock that increased ESG commonality among resource-constrained firms. Independently, we find that mimetic behavior, firms imitating peers within industries, also contributes to convergence in ESG practices. Further, we examine commonality across markets finding evidence of a distinct, global and regional component. We show that sustainability commonality drives return comovement and is linked to firm performance, highlighting its role as a systemic driver of financial and corporate outcomes. Our findings highlight the systemic nature of ESG and its relevance for investors and policymakers.

title: Skewness-Aware Performance Appraisal: Reconciling Firm-Level and Aggregate Portfolio Risk in Risk-Adjusted Return Measures

detail.title: Skewness-Aware Performance Appraisal: Reconciling Firm-Level and Aggregate Portfolio Risk in Risk-Adjusted Return Measures
detail.abstract: Standard risk-adjusted performance measures-the Sharpe, Treynor, Sortino, and appraisal ratios, along with their skewness-and kurtosis-adjusted extensions-are typically computed on the return series of the portfolio under evaluation, treating its higher moments as intrinsic to that portfolio alone. This paper argues that such treatment is incomplete once a well-documented empirical regularity is taken into account: firm-level stock returns are almost always positively skewed, while aggregate market returns are almost always negatively skewed, a gap that Albuquerque (2011) attributes to cross-sectional co-skewness among constituent returns rather than to the skewness of any individual holding. We show that this co-skewness term enters the adjusted Sharpe ratio of Pezier and White (2006) as a portfolio-level penalty that is invisible in, and unrelated to, the quality of the constituent securities a manager selects. This creates what we term a skewness reconciliation gap between manager-level stock-selection performance and portfoliolevel risk-adjusted performance. We derive this gap formally, show how it varies with the number of holdings and the degree of diversification, and propose an empirical decomposition protocol that separates a selection-implied adjusted Sharpe ratio from the realized, co-skewness-penalized one. We discuss implications for cross-manager performance comparison, incentive-fee design, and mean-variance-skewness portfolio construction.

title:
Ceremonial Compliance or Genuine Reform? 
Mandatory ESG Disclosure and Bank Credit Risk in India and China
affiliations: and Indian Institute of Management Calcutta

detail.title:
Ceremonial Compliance or Genuine Reform? 
Mandatory ESG Disclosure and Bank Credit Risk in India and China
detail.abstract: We examine whether mandatory ESG disclosure changes bank behaviour or only bank reporting. Our setting is India's Business Responsibility Report (BRR) mandate, which was extended to listed firms in steps set by market-capitalization rank (2013, 2016 and 2020). This staggered, rulebased rollout provides a natural experiment, which we study in a panel of 58 Indian and Chinese banks over 2012-2021, with Chinese banks serving as a never-treated benchmark. The mandate changed reporting. Treated banks' Bloomberg ESG disclosure scores rise by about three points; the response is persistent, builds over three years, and is concentrated in disclosure-intensive score components and among private banks that face capital-market scrutiny. The mandate did not change behaviour. Across fixed-effects, Mundlak and system-GMM specifications, disclosure has no within-bank effect on credit risk; the negative ESG-risk correlation reflects selection between banks, strongest among state-owned institutions; and in the long run disclosure rises with credit risk, a pattern consistent with reputation management rather than discipline. This configuration matches the joint prediction of ceremonial adoption (Meyer and Rowan, 1977) and a soft budget constraint (Kornai, 1986) that India's bank-rescue record shows to be system-wide. Disclosure mandates elicit reporting; behavioural change requires consequences.

title: Navigating the Writing Journey: Pedagogical Insights into Planning, Drafting, and Revising in English Language Teaching

detail.title: Navigating the Writing Journey: Pedagogical Insights into Planning, Drafting, and Revising in English Language Teaching
detail.abstract: The second language writing is a cognitive task which involves the coordination of linguistic, and metacognitive resources. The article is a detailed discussion of the process-focused approach to teaching writing. Going beyond the conventional emphasis on the final product, the paper divides the writing process to three critical stages of the writing process: strategic planning, fluency-based draft, and substantive revision. Moreover, the theoretical basis of these phases has been explored which present some evidence-based pedagogical techniques to use in the ELT classroom. Among the significant discourse, there are the techniques of applying bilingual scaffolding to lower-level students, the difference between global and surface-level editing. The positive application of ICT tools has been mentioned using digital collaborative tools to support feedback and group work. The main idea of this paper is a concept of recursion that underlines the idea of writing as a cyclic process, not a linear one. Attempt has been made to equip educators with the means of helping learners to become more autonomous and enhance the quality of his/her writing by addressing the most widespread issues namely writer's block and assessment pressures. Finally, it proposes the classroom atmosphere that glorifies the messiness of the creation process and turns the task of writing into a controllable and empowering process of communication among L2 learners.

detail.abstract: • This dissertation explores the relationship between Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and tax avoidance within neoliberal shareholder capitalism. Often viewed as contradictory, with CSR promoting social welfare while tax avoidance reduces public funding, both are mutually embedded, profit maximising strategies. Using the lens of global inequality, this paper traces their shared historical evolution from colonial times to modern practices. Through case studies of Amazon, Starbucks, and Nando's, it examines mechanisms like transfer pricing and intellectual property royalties. Ultimately, the essay concludes that CSR and tax avoidance act as complementary business strategies, raising profound ethical concerns regarding wealth distribution and democratic accountability.

detail.title:
Joint Licence Negotiation by Technology Implementers and Competition Law: Convergence between Japan and the European Union
 - Lessons from METI's Standard-Essential Patent Study and the EU's Revised Technology Transfer Guidelines -
detail.abstract:
Standard-essential patents ('SEPs') sit at the intersection of intellectual property law, which grants exclusive and strictly territorial rights, and competition law, which polices the exercise of market power. As SEP licensing has spread from electronics into automotive, industrial and other sectors, technology implementers have increasingly explored joint negotiation as a way of correcting information asymmetries and reducing transaction costs vis-à-vis patent holders bound by commitments to license on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory ('FRAND') terms. 

This paper examines two policy documents addressing that practice: Japan's 2021 interim report on the standard-essential patent licensing environment, published by the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry ('METI'), and the European Commission's 2026 revised Technology Transfer Guidelines, which for the first time provide dedicated guidance on 'Licensing Negotiation Groups' ('LNGs'). 

Although produced independently, nearly five years apart, by wholly different institutional actors, the two documents converge substantially in their underlying competition-law analysis. The paper argues that this convergence-real but only partial-illustrates why international alignment of competition-law treatment matters more for patent-related conduct than for most other regulatory subject matter, given the inherently territorial nature of patent rights and the irreducibly global character of standardisation and licensing markets.

title: Gender, Ecology, and Philosophy: Literary Dimensions of Indian Knowledge System Evolution

detail.title: Gender, Ecology, and Philosophy: Literary Dimensions of Indian Knowledge System Evolution
detail.abstract: The study is a theoretical one that explores the intersection of gender, ecology and philosophy in the changing Indian Knowledge System (IKS), which is examined in the dimensions of literature as an analysis tool. Based on textual analysis, hermeneutics, and comparative philosophy, the study follows the historical nature of IKS beginning with the ancient Vedic and epic periods when Prakriti as the creative force of femininity and earth as the mother reflect the entire related and connected nature, through the influence of medieval Bhakti-Sufi inclusivity, colonial destabilisations, and postcolonial reclaiming. Prakriti-Purusha duality, Dharma and Ahimsa are the main philosophical ideas, whose prismatic implementation reveals the anthropocentric tends transformed to eco-centric ones. With epics, Puranic myths, devotional poetry, and contemporary writers like Tagore, Roy, Devi and Ghosh, gendered agency, ecological piety, feminist redefinitions of fluidity (e.g., Ardhanarishvara) and environmental crisis and gender repression are reflected in literary narratives. Indigenous views are extensively incorporated into the analysis which, with the ecofeminist critiques, especially the regeneration of Prakriti by Vandana Shiva, and issues such as colonial legacies, globalisation, essentialism, and scarcely considered topics like queer ecology are addressed. Results provide insights into the flexibility and sustainability of IKS, providing an option to Western epistemologies in the face of global sustainability and equity issues.

title: Volatility Laundering in Private Credit: How Appraisal-Based Valuation Masks Economic Risk in Global Credit Markets

detail.title: Volatility Laundering in Private Credit: How Appraisal-Based Valuation Masks Economic Risk in Global Credit Markets
detail.abstract: Private credit has grown from roughly $250 billion in assets under management in 2008 to an estimated $2.28 trillion in 2025, with Preqin projecting $4.50 trillion by 2030. The asset class has been sold on a proposition that deserves more scrutiny than it typically gets: equity-like income with bond-like, or better, volatility. This paper argues that a meaningful share of that stability is an artifact of how private credit is valued rather than evidence of genuinely lower economic risk. Extending a critique Cliff Asness developed for private equity and named volatility laundering, the paper builds an original conceptual model, the Volatility Laundering Framework, formalizing how illiquidity, Level 3 classification, quarterly appraisal cycles, manager discretion, and thin secondary markets compress reported volatility, inflate Sharpe ratios, understate Value-at-Risk, and delay loss recognition. Its central contribution is that this mechanism runs differently in credit than in equity: because loan cash flows are capped on the upside, smoothing in private credit functions primarily as loss deferral rather than the two-sided smoothing documented in private equity. The argument rests on verifiable, current evidence: Fitch's record 9.2 percent private credit default rate for 2025, Proskauer's finding that covenant-lite deal share rose from 4 to 21 percent between 2023 and 2025, business development companies trading at 14 to 20 percent discounts to net asset value through mid-2026, and the November 2025 collapse of Blue Owl's proposed merger of two of its own credit funds, which briefly forced a roughly 20 percent gap between one fund's appraised value and the market's assessment of the other into public view. The paper also reports an original Monte Carlo simulation of portfolio credit losses and a stylized illustration of return smoothing, both fully specified and reproducible. It closes with implications for institutional investors, pension funds, insurers, and family offices, and an assessment of the regulatory response now underway at the SEC, the DOL, IOSCO, and the Financial Stability Board.

title: Authenticity Considerations in Strategic Games
affiliations: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV) (Formerly University of Texas-Pan American) - Economics and Finance

detail.title: Authenticity Considerations in Strategic Games
detail.abstract: We develop a framework in which individuals value both material outcomes and authenticity. The latter is captured through selfcongruence (the alignment between actions and underlying values) and social recognition (the extent to which others correctly infer that alignment). Self-congruence can act as an internal commitment device that alters equilibrium behavior, while recognition concerns independently affect incentives. Our analysis identifies welfare effects arising from both equilibrium selection and the accurate recognition of motives. The model provides a tractable way to incorporate authenticity into strategic interaction.

title: Market-Based Finance: Its Contributions and Emerging Issues
affiliations: and Bank for International Settlements

detail.title: Market-Based Finance: Its Contributions and Emerging Issues
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the structural transformation of traditional banking into a global, market-based financial system. Driven by financial engineering and globalisation, Market-Based Finance (MBF) offers comparative advantages through enhanced funding diversification, specialized risk management, and systemic competition. Our analysis demonstrates that while MBF acts as a vital economic "spare tyre" and constrains traditional banking inefficiencies, it introduces complex, systemic vulnerabilities. Furthermore, we find that regulatory arbitrage was not the primary driver of MBF’s expansion, though the ecosystem remains dynamic with peripheral products continually entering its perimeter. Finally, the paper highlights that unsolved market failures and information gaps persist. To ensure systemic stability and effective conduct regulation, regulatory authorities require broader and deeper access to data to evaluate and mitigate potential risks.

title: Momentum across the Capital Structure

detail.title: Momentum across the Capital Structure
detail.abstract: We develop and empirically test theoretical conditions for time-series momentum (TSM) and reversal across the capital structure. The conditions organize a unified pattern of predictability: equity TSM is concentrated in high-risk firms, low-risk firms reverse, corporate bonds reverse, and past equity returns predict future bond returns. The mechanism arises in a model where equity is a call option on firm assets and variance risk is priced. Variance risk generates momentum, leverage generates reversal, and the former dominates in sufficiently levered or high-variance firms. Aggregating these firm-level forces at the portfolio level explains and predicts cross-sectional momentum crashes.

detail.abstract: Traditional financial literacy education often reflects what academics deem important rather than what individual investors actively seek to learn. detail.abstract: Amid the unregulated spread of artificial intelligence tools in Bangladeshi K-12 education, public fear over data misuse, algorithmic bias, and teacher replacement has surged. At the same time, national policy remains devoid of mandatory algorithmic audits, impact assessments, or public registries. This study constructs an evidence-based blueprint to replace panic with accountable governance. A sequential mixed-methods design integrated policy document analysis, a 230-respondent survey of teachers, parents, and education officers, content coding of 100 media items, Right to Information requests, 22 semi-structured interviews, and four case studies, benchmarked against international frameworks including the EU AI Act, NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and UNESCO guidance. Findings revealed a stark perception-reality gap: 78% of parents reported high worry, yet 94% of respondents had never witnessed an AI-related incident, and no AI tool deployed in schools had undergone an algorithmic audit. Media coverage was 73% fear-framed, with social media as the dominant information source. Stakeholders overwhelmingly rejected blanket bans, with 34% prioritising mandatory safety audits, 28% demanding a strict children's data protection law, and 22% calling for compulsory AI literacy training. Drawing on this evidence, the article proposes a five-pillar national policy blueprint: (1) mandatory Algorithmic Impact Assessments before procurement, (2) a public national registry of assessed tools, (3) a Children's Educational Data Protection Code, (4) universal AI literacy for teachers and students, and (5) equity-first infrastructure requirements. The blueprint offers a rights-based, auditable, and phased pathway from panic to evidence-driven governance, directly translating stakeholder demands and international best practice into a coherent regulatory architecture for Bangladesh.

title: How Problematic are Persistent Budget Deficits? Monetary Sovereignty, Efficiency, and the Inflation Margin

detail.abstract: Are persistent budget deficits problematic? Modern Monetary Theory answers that it depends on monetary sovereignty. We test this in a five-year-window panel of up to 200 countries (1960-2024), regressing forward growth and world-frontier decomposition components on fiscal balances interacted with de facto sovereignty (Ilzetzki et al., 2019). The results are disciplining. Growth-level associations are fragile and concentrated in upper conditional quantiles; an apparent efficiency-channel sovereignty offset is downgraded to suggestive under frontier-re-estimating bootstrap inference; event-study, long-run advancedeconomy, and deficit-dynamics designs show no regime differential, and deficit dynamics are dominated by mean reversion. Even the inflation margin-MMT's own stated constraintsurvives only in a qualified form: the deficit-inflation link is concentrated in freely-falling regimes, with no detectable differential among stable floaters. The employment margin fares better: sovereign deficits predict relatively lower subsequent unemployment, a differential that strengthens under the narrow coding and survives first-differencing at the 10% level. We document a data-provenance failure in a widely used WEO mirror and retract one threshold claim. Estimates are conditional correlations, not causal effects. A companion paper (Levkoff, 2026) develops the frontier-measurement methodology used here.

title: Testing For Cycle-Dependent Loss Development in Long-Tail Casualty Business

detail.title: Testing For Cycle-Dependent Loss Development in Long-Tail Casualty Business
detail.abstract: Reserving methods in the chain-ladder tradition treat the development of paid and case-incurred losses as invariant to the state of the underwriting cycle, although practitioners widely believe that soft-market accident years develop more adversely. This paper tests the proposition directly: development factors are regressed on observable, accident-year-dated market covariates within a lognormal development-factor model that nests the cycle-blind chain ladder. The test uses the two public CAS Schedule P compilations: 426 company-line triangles with realized runoff , accident years 1988-2007, a span containing the 2001-2004 hard market. Raw premium growth appears associated with development, but a placebo line, rate-regulated private passenger auto, exposes the association as trend contamination. De-trended, the pooled cycle coefficient is indistinguishable from zero in both eras and both bases (pooled 1988-2007: 0.0016, s.e. 0.0025), vanishes entirely under calendar-year controls, and is confirmed null by hierarchical Bayesian re-estimation. What replicates across eras is cross-sectional: companies growing faster than their line develop adversely. The reserving cycle, in its loss-development form, fails a powered, placebo-disciplined test; where cycle effects on reserves exist, they must be sought in estimate behaviour or finer price data, not in the development of the losses.

Using data from the National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics, insights from a roundtable convened by the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, and my own experience in the field, I examine demographic patterns and the conditions under which doctoral training in economics becomes a viable or exclusionary pathway to professional mobility. Particular attention is paid to the underrepresentation of U.S.-born students, especially those from certain racial or ethnic backgrounds, in economics doctoral programs. detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether the five classical stock return factors (i.e., market, size, value, profitability, and momentum) still have the announced alphas after 2010 and remain statistically significant when trading costs are considered realistically. Using pre-registered hypotheses, Harvey-Liu-Zhu significance framework (t ≥ 3.0), and empirical transaction costs from Novy-Marx & Velikov (2014), the findings show: (1) out of six factors, five have decayed after 2010 and both value and size premiums have even changed their signs; (2) when empirically-measured transaction costs are applied, only the market premium remains statistically significant; (3) the market premium has survived and strengthened, which suggests persistent fundamentals in risk versus statistical illusion in anomaly premiums.

detail.abstract: This paper explores how pension governance can be redefined by placing participants at its core, against the backdrop of ongoing Dutch pension reforms. Although legislative changes have primarily focused on contract design and financial sustainability, governance arrangements may fall short if they do not adequately reflect participants' evolving expectations and engagement. Using the framework of financial intermediation, we identify how pension providers create value for participants and society. We argue that governance structures must integrate transparency, adaptability, and participant voice to sustain their license to operate-financially, socially, and politically. Ten guiding principles are derived to strengthen governance and align outcomes with participants' needs. With these principles four governance frameworks emerge-Accept or Go, Engaged, SharedSay, and Voice & Choice-showing a progression from no participant influence to full co-determination in governance and product design, enabled by technology and tailored preferences. We conclude that participant-centered governance is feasible and necessary. It strengthens trust, aligns outcomes with expectations, and supports the long-term legitimacy of collective pensions in a changing social contract.

title: The Case for Mandatory AI Ethics Audits in Government Utilization:  A Philosophical and Bipartisan Call to Keep the (Human) Humanity in the Loop

detail.title: The Case for Mandatory AI Ethics Audits in Government Utilization:  A Philosophical and Bipartisan Call to Keep the (Human) Humanity in the Loop
detail.abstract:
The accelerating institutional adoption of artificial intelligence has produced a critical governance deficit: AI systems now exercise consequential decision-making authority across financial, legal, medical, and social domains, yet no standardized, operationally enforceable ethics audit framework governs their behavior. Existing regulatory instruments including the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, the EU AI Act, and ISO/IEC 42001 provide risk classification and design guidance but do not specify the procedural audit standards necessary to assess AI system compliance in practice.

This white paper proposes an AI Ethics Audit Framework derived from four decades of fiduciary law, federal regulatory practice, and institutional crisis management. Anchored in the fiduciary obligations of loyalty, prudence, care, and disclosure, principles with deep roots in U.S. banking regulation, SEC compliance, and receivership law, the framework translates legally established ethical obligations into five operational audit control domains: transparency, accountability, fairness, harm avoidance, and regulatory compliance.

The paper argues that fiduciary law offers the most institutionally mature and legally defensible architecture for AI ethics auditing, providing auditors, compliance officers, and regulators with a vocabulary and methodology already embedded in U.S. legal and financial governance infrastructure. Drawing on case studies from FDIC receivership practice, complex litigation advisory, and AI policy literature, the paper presents a structured audit methodology, a proposed control framework, and a phased implementation roadmap applicable across enterprise, public sector, and regulated industry contexts.

Findings suggest that organizations adopting structured AI ethics audit programs demonstrate measurably stronger regulatory positioning, reduced liability exposure, and enhanced stakeholder trust. Policy implications include recommendations for federal AI audit mandates, professional certification standards, and academic curriculum integration.

title: Talking to Digital Twins: Selective Disclosure and Belief Measurement in Financial Social Media

detail.title: Talking to Digital Twins: Selective Disclosure and Belief Measurement in Financial Social Media
detail.abstract: Social media affect financial markets, but public posts by financial media personas are voluntary disclosures. What is not disclosed is therefore usually unobserved. We address this measurement problem by conducting repeated, real-time interviews of "digital twins" built from monitored finfluencers' X accounts under a fixed protocol. The interviews recover stocklevel public-persona belief proxies even when no public recommendation is made. Because the interviews are generated and archived before the relevant return windows, the design avoids the look-ahead bias that arises when LLMs are queried ex post. The evidence shows that information obtained from these digital-twin interviews predicts the cross section of large-cap stock returns in the expected direction. Repeated real-time interviews therefore show how selective disclosure can be turned into measurable panels of market views.

detail.abstract: Europe’s competitiveness debate is increasingly centred on productivity growth. Recent reports by Mario Draghi, Enrico Letta and the European Commission identify weak productivity performance as the principal explanation for Europe’s widening economic gap with the United States. Yet, discussions of merger policy rarely engage systematically with the modern productivity literature. This paper argues that such an omission is increasingly difficult to justify. Contemporary research identifies four principal sources of productivity growth: product innovation, process innovation, diffusion and resource reallocation. While innovation remains essential, a growing body of evidence suggests that diffusion and reallocation play a central role in explaining differences in economic performance across firms, industries and countries. Europe’s competitiveness challenge appears increasingly linked to weaknesses in these latter mechanisms, rather than to a simple shortage of invention. The paper argues that mergers affect all four sources of productivity growth and that merger policy should therefore be evaluated through a broader dynamic framework. Such a framework would preserve the traditional objectives of competition policy, while incorporating a richer understanding of the mechanisms that generate long-run prosperity.

title: Scale Mixture EM for Horseshoe Mixtures of Experts
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and George Mason University

detail.title: Scale Mixture EM for Horseshoe Mixtures of Experts
detail.abstract: We develop an estimation algorithm for mixtures of experts in which both the expert coefficients and the gating network carry horseshoe priors. The key observation is that three separate latent structures, namely the allocation indicators, the Pólya-Gamma variables of the logistic gate, and the local and global scales of the horseshoe, are all variance-mean scale mixtures. Augmenting all three simultaneously turns every conditional maximisation step into a weighted least squares solve available in closed form. The resulting Scale Mixture EM algorithm, SM-HS-MoE, has no learning rate, no momentum schedule and no step size to tune. We establish monotonicity of the observed data objective under an explicit ordering of the conditional maximisation steps, and we characterise the local linear rate of convergence as the spectral radius of a missing information ratio that decomposes additively across the three augmentations. This decomposition predicts the algorithm's failure mode, namely that convergence slows precisely when experts overlap and allocation is uncertain, and we confirm it numerically: the observed rate is linear in allocation entropy with slope 0.40, falling to a floor of 0.82 set by the other two augmentations rather than to zero. On synthetic ill-conditioned problems with p = 200 predictors, SM-HS-MoE attains 19.7% excess test error over the oracle against 57.5% for Adam tuned by learning rate grid search, with higher routing accuracy and lower wall clock time inclusive of the grid. We also report a negative result. The horseshoe gate does not induce balanced expert utilisation and does not displace the auxiliary load balancing losses used in sparse mixture-ofexperts training. It thins the tail of the load distribution but leaves the coefficient of variation of expert loads essentially unchanged.

title: When Merit Promotes Cooperation: Prize Inequality in Intergroup Public-goods Competition
affiliations: ,  and Brown University, Students

detail.title: When Merit Promotes Cooperation: Prize Inequality in Intergroup Public-goods Competition
detail.abstract: This paper reports a laboratory experiment on how the source of rank assignment shapes the effect of prize inequality on cooperation. In a repeated public-goods game with intergroup competition, groups compete for a prize that is divided unequally within the winning group. A 2 × 2 design varies whether ranks are assigned by luck or earned through a memory task, and whether prize inequality is mild or extreme. Extreme inequality lowers contributions when ranks are assigned by luck, but this negative effect is offset and reverses in point estimates when ranks are earned. Thus, merit-based rank assignment changes how prize inequality affects intragroup cooperation in intergroup competition.

title: The Binary Hedge Frontier: Prediction-Market Claims and Event-State Risk in Portfolio Theory A Theory of Event-Basis Risk, Binary Hedgeability, and Incomplete-Market Portfolio Design

detail.title: The Binary Hedge Frontier: Prediction-Market Claims and Event-State Risk in Portfolio Theory A Theory of Event-Basis Risk, Binary Hedgeability, and Incomplete-Market Portfolio Design
detail.abstract: A binary prediction-market claim pays according to whether an event occurs; a portfolio loses money according to the magnitude of that event's consequences. These are different objects, and the gap between them has no general treatment in portfolio theory. This paper develops one. Using the law of total variance, we decompose portfolio risk into a between-state component generated by the occurrence of an event and a within-state component generated by the severity of its consequences. We show that a binary event claim can span only the between-state component, and we introduce the Binary Hedgeability Ratio (BHR)-the share of portfolio variance attributable to the event partition-and prove that it equals both the squared correlation between the portfolio return and the event indicator and the maximum fractional variance reduction achievable by any position in the claim. The residual is event-basis risk: the part of portfolio loss that no binary claim can hedge. We then define the Binary Hedge Frontier, the mean-variance frontier augmented by binary state claims treated as non-Gaussian, incompletemarket assets, and we separate three objects routinely conflated in the literature: the physical event probability π, the market-implied price p m E , and the portfolio loss conditional on the event. Four propositions follow: a hedgeability bound, a non-spanning condition, a price-probability separation, and a tail-asymmetry result showing that a variance-minimizing binary hedge can raise expected shortfall. We give a regression-based empirical design built on event-probability changes, together with a calibrated simulation that illustrates the theory. The framework characterizes when prediction-market claims are hedges, when they are merely forecasts, and when they may manufacture false hedge confidence.

detail.abstract: This paper tests whether the Adaptive Sovereign Balance Framework (ASBF) — introduced as a diagnostic of the sovereign balance's functional configuration in a companion paper on Kazakhstan (2005-2023) — reproduces under transfer to a second commodity-dependent economy, Chile (2005-2023). The five-contour architecture, the F/V/D/R operationalisation chain, and the two-index diagnostic plane (SVI^S , SVI^P) carry over structurally unchanged. Three lines of evidence are assessed. Statistical discrimination of SVI^P between stress and calm years does not reach significance at the available sample size (Mann-Whitney p=0.368; Fisher exact p=0.758; permutation p=0.195; n=16) — a result attributed to a smaller and more heterogeneous shock sample than Kazakhstan's, not to a failure of the diagnostic object itself. Lag-time comparison against IMF Article IV assessments across three episodes shows SVI^P registering positive pressure ahead of each crisis, including a signal-year value (+1.16, 2007) closely matching Kazakhstan's (+1.020). Robustness checks — an honest out-of-sample test (5 of 5 years, 2019-2023) and a crosscountry panel check (14 of 16 years) — probe distinct vulnerabilities of the weighting construction and both return negative for overfitting. The paper also identifies an unresolved methodological fork: Chile's and Kazakhstan's contour weights are computed by different normalisation formulas, which leaves one of Article 1's central predictions untestable until comparability is established. The transfer is read as necessary but not sufficient evidence for generalisability, bounded to the class of small open economies with a sovereign fund of comparable function. Large language models (Claude, Anthropic) were used to assist with drafting, language editing, and calculation cross-checking, while the research design, theoretical framework, and all substantive conclusions are the author’s own.

title: Buy, Borrow, and Sell Anyway: Insider Share Pledging and The Limits Of Buy-borrow-Die

detail.title: Buy, Borrow, and Sell Anyway: Insider Share Pledging and The Limits Of Buy-borrow-Die
detail.abstract: In the "buy-borrow-die" account of top-end taxation, the wealthy borrow against appreciated stock instead of selling it, deferring tax until the basis step-up at death erases the gain. The borrowing itself has never been measured at the top. Since 2006, SEC proxy statements must disclose, by name, the shares their directors and named executives have pledged as loan collateral, and they also report blockholder pledges that could shift control; we extract every such disclosure from every proxy statement filed over 2007-2022 and link each pledger to their complete trading record. Pledged collateral peaks at $155 billion in 2021 and is hyper-concentrated: one holder accounts for seventeen percent of it and a hundred holders for more than two-thirds, a Gini of 0.93. Yet the behavior the account predicts does not appear. Pledgers realize gains at the same rate whether pledged or not, show no significant gradient in the tax incentive to defer, and do not defer when rates rise. Nor are pledgers the never-selling type the story describes: compared with non-pledging insiders at the same firms and of the same size, they are seven to eleven percentage points less likely never to sell. What tracks pledging is instead the cost of credit. These are facts about disclosed insiders, the one population whose pledging and trading are both observable, and the population the debate itself names. Among them, borrowing against stock looks like a credit instrument rather than the tax-deferral engine the debate assumes.

title: Refutation-resistant Beliefs

detail.title: Refutation-resistant Beliefs
detail.abstract: Beliefs often shape the very data used to evaluate them. We study a minimax refutation-resistance criterion that ranks misspecified beliefs by worst-case prediction error at their own induced action. In a linear two-activity model, the unique refutation-resistant belief equalizes inputs, is fully refutation-resistant, and coincides with the unique payoff-pessimistic belief, i.e., the belief minimizing predicted payoff. We then characterize the environments in which this equivalence between refutation resistance and payoff pessimism extends beyond the linear benchmark, and show that refutation resistance hinges on the existence of actions at which candidate technologies generate identical payoff predictions. This diagnostic structure allows us to delineate technology classes for which fully refutation-resistant beliefs exist and to identify when such beliefs are necessarily payoff-pessimistic.

detail.title: Skin Color at Work
detail.abstract: Do politically active economic elites reproduce racial and color hierarchies inside the private firms they own or operate? We address this question by linking Brazilian electoral records to a continuous, photograph-based Skin Color Index and matched employer-employee administrative data from RAIS, allowing us to compare workers employed within the same firm and municipality-year who differ in their skin-tone position relative to the firm owner. Workers whose skin tone differs from the owner's earn wages that are 3.1 to 3.3 percent lower and accumulate about 5 percent less tenure. Using a continuous measure of relative skin tone, we also find that workers who are darker than the owner earn lower wages and face a higher probability of separation. These penalties are especially pronounced among college-educated workers: the return to a college degree is substantially smaller when worker and owner differ in skin tone and declines further as the worker becomes darker relative to the owner. Consistent with Becker's theory of taste-based discrimination, stronger local product-market competition attenuates the wage penalty associated with worker-owner skin-tone differences, although it also reduces tenure among non-aligned worker-owner pairs. The findings suggest that racial inequality is reproduced not only through public policy or political representation, but also through the private employment relationships controlled by politically active economic elites.

detail.abstract: Frontier AI laboratories are proprietary, and the most granular evidence on the automation of their own research and engineering is what they choose to publish. This paper develops a disciplined way of using such evidence and applies it to the eleven quantitative series reported in Anthropic's 2026 article When AI Builds Itself. We admit the reported numbers while excluding the accompanying narrative, fit minimal-assumption models to each series, and derive economic implications through standard production, demand, and equilibrium theory. Three results organise the analysis. First, the automated and human components of research output behave as near-perfect complements, an assumption tested rather than estimated, so aggregate acceleration is governed by Amdahl-Baumol dynamics; under a stated common-frontier assumption, a joint restriction on two independently fitted series identifies the residual human task as the heavy tail of the task-length distribution, and the equilibrium pays it a rapidly rising scarcity rent. Second, market demand for software output along the observed path is elastic, so total expenditure rises even as unit costs collapse. Third, the binding constraint, and with it the rent, passes from human judgment to compute capacity at a derived regime change: May 2029 at the fitted parameters, with the sequence of regimes considerably more robust than the calendar date. We characterise which conclusions survive strategic misreporting by the source, propagate the source's stated imprecision into interval estimates, and derive testable implications, the earliest of which can be checked during 2026.

detail.title: The Plague and the Protectorate: A Materialistic Framework for State-Building during the Early Origins of Islam
detail.abstract: This paper provides a materialistic framework for the early origins of Islam, examining how the catastrophic demographic shocks of sixth-and seventh-century plague pandemics created a massive governance vacuum in the Near East. We argue that early Islamic expansion and institutional design are best understood not through a lens of predatory extraction or a "protection racket," but as a sophisticated process of primary state-building. By leveraging a unified, ecumenical ideological framework, the early Caliphate successfully monopolized violence, drastically reduced transaction costs across fractured trade routes, and centralized taxation through Zakat to fund vital public goods. Rather than acting as a parasitic entity, the nascent Islamic polity functioned as a rational institutional response to systemic regional collapse, substituting localized anarchy with a centralized, high-capacity state capable of sustainable territorial and economic integration.

detail.abstract: Short dated Bitcoin binary contracts settle over horizons brief enough that expected drift is negligible, which reduces their fair value to a function of current spot and short horizon volatility alone. This paper frames the contract as a cash or nothing digital option, derives a driftless fair value, and defines an entry rule that acts when the implied price and fair value differ by at least a fixed buffer, sizing by a model edge score. On 182 resolved contracts traded across 22 to 23 June 2026, the rule realised a positive statistical edge, a win rate of 67.6 percent against the 63 percent break even rate implied by the mean entry price of 0.63, an edge of 4.6 percentage points. The point estimates are positive across the headline measures, but the sample is too small to establish significance: bootstrap intervals on the edge include zero, and the model fair value does not improve on the market price as a probability forecast. The realised gain is concentrated in a small number of trades and coincides with a directional position, and an edge threshold selection rule does not persist out of sample. The result is interpreted as a statistical edge documented within a single window, whose significance and source, a genuine pricing signal against the established favorite longshot bias, remain open questions pending a larger sample. The contribution is the pricing framework and its evaluation.

detail.abstract: Does pedestrian foot traffic cause crime? Using the universe of 2018-2019 Chicago road closures, I show that closures attracting pedestrians (festivals, block parties) raise foot traffic by about 61% and cause a 59% increase in outdoor crime on the closed block, with no significant displacement to neighbors and no effect on indoor or residential crime. detail.abstract: Bangladesh's leather industry has remained trapped near US$1 billion in annual exports for more than a decade despite an abundant supply of internationally valued raw hides, while Vietnam-which imports most of the leather it processes-exports around US$27 billion of footwear and leather goods each year. This article employs a qualitative comparative policy analysis to explain this underperformance and to identify a more effective development pathway. Drawing on the experience of Vietnam, China, India, Italy, and Brazil, and on Bangladesh's own ready-made garment industry, it argues that the sector's central problem is one of sequencing: successive policies treated upstream environmental compliance and tannery modernization as prerequisites for downstream growth, postponing the manufacturing expansion that could have financed industrial upgrading. The article proposes a three-track strategy-immediate expansion of footwear and leather goods manufacturing using imported certified leather where necessary, parallel reform of tanning infrastructure and hide collection, and long-term investment in design, branding, and innovation. It concludes that a US$10 billion export sector by 2035 is plausible, but conditional on institutional coordination and disciplined execution rather than resource endowment.

detail.title: When Search Undermines Cooperation
detail.abstract: This paper studies endogenous search and cooperation in repeated relationships. Search improves matching but facilitates rematching, weakening separation as punishment and reducing cooperation. High-and low-search equilibria can coexist, with low search sustaining greater cooperation and welfare. Welfare differences reflect cooperation, matching-composition, and search-cost effects. An interior mixed equilibrium may exist and outperform low search. Stochastic selection depends on basin size rather than welfare; under coevolution, pure equilibria are locally stable, whereas an interior equilibrium is unstable under an upward-crossing condition. A planner may prefer universal high search despite decentralized welfare inferiority. The mechanism extends to general matching technologies.

detail.abstract:
Household consumption has traditionally been modelled as a function of income, with the Keynesian consumption function providing the foundation for understanding the relationship between income, consumption, and savings. Although this framework has played a central role in macroeconomic analysis, it does not explicitly distinguish between expenditure required to satisfy functional needs and expenditure arising from behavioural and marketing influences. This paper proposes the Functional Utility Cost Gap (FUCG) Framework, a conceptual extension that integrates Keynesian consumption theory with consumer psychology, marketing, and household finance.

The framework introduces the concept of minimum functional consumption, defined as the minimum expenditure required to obtain a given level of functional utility, and distinguishes it from actual household consumption. The difference between the two is termed the Functional Utility Cost Gap (FUCG), representing expenditure incurred beyond functional requirements. The framework further decomposes the FUCG into two components: FUCG₁, arising from non-persuasive behavioural factors such as bounded rationality, habits, convenience, limited information, and financial illiteracy, and FUCG₂, arising from persuasive marketing activities including advertising, branding, emotional appeals, social influence, and promotional strategies.

The study also distinguishes between informational marketing and persuasive marketing, arguing that these two forms of marketing influence household consumption through fundamentally different mechanisms. Informational marketing improves consumer decision-making by reducing information asymmetry and lowering the minimum expenditure required to obtain functional utility, thereby increasing consumption efficiency. Persuasive marketing, in contrast, encourages expenditure beyond functional requirements, widens the Functional Utility Cost Gap, and reduces household savings.

Building upon this behavioural decomposition, the paper derives corresponding consumption and saving functions and presents a graphical representation illustrating the relationships among income, consumption, savings, and break-even income levels. The framework further establishes a conceptual link between microeconomic consumer behaviour and Keynesian macroeconomics by demonstrating how persuasive marketing simultaneously influences household financial efficiency and aggregate demand. At the household level, persuasive marketing may reduce savings and increase expenditure without proportionate gains in functional utility. However, when aggregated across households, the resulting increase in consumption contributes to higher aggregate demand, output, employment, and short-run economic growth, thereby highlighting a trade-off between microeconomic financial efficiency and macroeconomic performance.

The proposed framework contributes to the literature by providing an integrated conceptual model that combines insights from Keynesian economics, consumer psychology, marketing, and household finance. By decomposing household consumption into functional and behavioural components, the Functional Utility Cost Gap framework offers a new perspective for analysing consumer expenditure, household savings, marketing effectiveness, and the interaction between individual financial decision-making and macroeconomic outcomes. The framework also provides a foundation for future empirical research and policy analysis concerning consumer behaviour, household financial well-being, and marketing practices.

title: Closing the Golden Door: How U.S. Policy Changes Toward International Students Have Reshaped Higher Education, the Labor Market, and the American Economy

detail.title: Closing the Golden Door: How U.S. Policy Changes Toward International Students Have Reshaped Higher Education, the Labor Market, and the American Economy
detail.abstract: International students have long served as a self-funding engine of American economic growth, scientific leadership, and geopolitical influence. In the 2024-25 academic year they contributed $42.9 billion to the U.S. economy and supported 355,736 jobs (NAFSA, 2025a). Two waves of restrictive policy, the first from 2017 to 2020 and a far more aggressive second wave beginning in January 2025, have turned this durable national advantage into a measurable and accelerating loss. This paper synthesizes federal enrollment and visa data, economic modeling by NAFSA and JB International, innovation research by the National Foundation for American Policy, court records, and survey evidence to trace the effects of these policy changes across five dimensions: the national economy, university finances, the labor market and corporate innovation, individual psychological well-being, and the global competitive position of the United States. A case study of Indiana University Bloomington, where international enrollment fell 11.2 percent in a single year and contributed to a $25.9 million one-semester loss for the state of Indiana, illustrates how national policy translates into local damage. The realized losses are already historic. New enrollment collapsed 17 percent in fall 2025, costing $1.1 billion in spending and roughly 23,000 jobs in one semester. The prospective losses are larger still, with scenario modeling placing the long-run cost of losing one third of international STEM students at $240 to $481 billion in GDP annually. The paper concludes that the damage is substantially self-inflicted, partly irreversible, and concentrated in the sectors on which American prosperity most depends.

However, despite the growing number of internet users and the use of various technological advancements, most SMEs in the country have remained limited to conducting only basic digital activities such as marketing and communication. detail.abstract: We examine whether private firm disclosure affects the price that public firms pay for their bank loans. Using global data on syndicated loans, we find that private firm disclosure significantly reduces public firms' loan spreads. This finding supports a positive information externalities view whereby private firm disclosure helps banks evaluate public borrowers' credit risk within the industry context and reduces information asymmetry between banks and borrowers. Consistent with this mechanism, we find larger reductions in public firms' loan spreads when banks have less information about the borrower or lower expected monitoring intensity, when public-firm borrowers are more informationally opaque, when private firms have greater economic importance in the industry, when private and public firms are more economically similar, or when a larger share of private firms in an industry have audited financial statements. We show that private firm disclosure generates positive externalities for the loan market by reducing information asymmetry.

detail.abstract: The national economy's structural dependence on oil revenues. This study proposes a machine learning framework for cross-market dependency analysis between global oil market indicators and the stock prices of major Iranian refinery companies listed on the Tehran Stock Exchange. Historical data, including Brent crude oil price, oil trading volume, exchange rate, and temporal variables, were collected and integrated into a unified dataset covering approximately eight years of trading activity. Three machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest Regression, XGBoost Regression, and Polynomial Regression, were evaluated and compared using the R² score and RMSE metrics. The findings indicate that global oil market variables contain substantial predictive information regarding the behaviour of Iranian refinery stocks and can support data-driven investment analysis in energy-dependent financial markets.

title:

Statutes of Repose, the Missing Inspector, and a Knowledge Gate for the People who Design Things

detail.title:
Design Accountability: 
Statutes of Repose, the Missing Inspector, and a Knowledge Gate for the People who Design Things
detail.abstract: Statutes of repose extinguish claims against the designers and builders of things a fixed number of years after completion, regardless of discovery, culpability, or concealment. This Article argues that the doctrine does something worse than deny stale claims: it subsidizes a design strategy. A hazard engineered to fail slowly, hidden where no user can inspect it, will predictably outlast the repose window, and the designer who conceals best is the designer the statute protects most completely. The Article proceeds from a specimen, a Pennsylvania home whose garage slab was built over a concealed void on a single unprotected steel column that corroded for thirty years behind a sealed wall, and generalizes. First, it shows that the finality rationales for repose, lost evidence, faded memory, and fair notice, each collapse when the defendant manufactured the evidentiary silence, and that limitations doctrine already recognizes this through a fraudulent concealment exception that repose alone lacks. Second, it demonstrates that the resulting incentive is not hypothetical by assembling the documented record of design decision concealment across industries: automotive cost benefit suppression, tobacco and asbestos knowledge management, pharmaceutical ghost management, aviation certification concealment, and the built environment itself. Third, it shows that American law already operates downstream harm surveillance in food, motor vehicles, drugs and devices, consumer products, and workplaces, under the closely regulated industry doctrine and mandatory death and injury reporting, and that housing is the conspicuous omission. Drawing on the builder provisions of the Code of Hammurabi as the ancient baseline of unlimited accountability, the Article proposes a knowledge gate as a domain agnostic principle of design accountability: time based liability shields should shelter what could not have been known at the moment of the design decision despite reasonable diligence, and should shelter nothing that was known and concealed. Two transplant reforms follow: a fraudulent concealment carve out in statutes of repose, and early warning reporting for the built environment on the model of 49 U.S.C. § 30166 and Florida's post collapse milestone inspection statute.

title: The Logic and Consequences of Equalizing Bureaucratic Recruitment: Evidence from the 1073 Examination Reform in Song China

detail.title: The Logic and Consequences of Equalizing Bureaucratic Recruitment: Evidence from the 1073 Examination Reform in Song China
detail.abstract: We study how equalizing opportunities for bureaucratic recruitment reshapes politics in distinct stages. Initially, it brings more officials from humble backgrounds into the bureaucracy. Their lack of patronage ties, however, limits prospects for career advancement and thus motivates them to seek promotion by displaying exceptional loyalty and zeal in carrying out the ruler's preferred policies, often with downstream effects on governance and social stability. We test this argument using a reform of the civil service examinations in Northern Song China (960-1127), which shifted from literary composition to formulaic interpretation of the Confucian classics, a change that favored candidates from modest backgrounds. The reform increased the presence of nonelite bureaucrats whose hometowns had greater access to printed books. These officials extracted more revenue as prefects, were increasingly assigned to posts implementing the ruler's agenda, pursued the ruler's preferred policies with greater intensity, and faced higher rates of rebellion.

detail.abstract: Japan's indirect transmission rights (ITR) pay holders the day-ahead price spread between adjacent zones. Settlement is capped at the holder's own physical spot transactions, and no secondary market exists. A March 2025 government review found auction clearing prices persistently below realized spreads. Its remedy raises the auction's 0.01 yen/kWh minimum offer price from FY2026. We quantify and decompose the gap using all 2,306 weekly products auctioned between FY2019 and FY2026. Contracted rights returned buyers 0.30 to 0.53 yen/kWh over the price paid, depending on the settlement bound. Outcomes are tail-driven, and the median product roughly broke even. The discount is structural rather than a floor problem alone. Clearing prices respond to observable ex-ante congestion risk with 43-50% of the slope at which spreads realize. The shortfall concentrates in competitively priced products, which carry three times the deficit of floor-priced ones. Supply is released mechanically, and settlement rules foreclose purely financial participation, so no arbitrage capital can close the gap. The discount is an equilibrium feature of a hedger-only auction with thin demand. This supports the review's participation diagnosis but not its price-floor remedy. Early FY2026 data show fewer floor clearings and no improvement against the pre-2025 baseline. detail.abstract: This paper examines the economy-wide impacts of Indonesia's electric vehicle (EV) transition using a recursive dynamic computable general equilibrium (CGE) model calibrated to a 185-sector Indonesian social accounting matrix.
